Expectation1: Enforcing the law and maintaining public order
Situation1: An armed robbery is in progress, posing immediate threat to lives and property
Expectation2: Raise public awareness about social inequities and marginalized groups
Situation2: They respond to an urgent incident of discrimination that requires immediate public attention and awareness.
Story: The radio crackled with urgency as I sped toward the scene of an armed robbery, my police badge heavy on my chest. The dispatcher’s voice was tense—shots fired, civilians in danger. My training screamed at me to focus, to enforce the law, to protect lives at all costs. But as I neared the intersection, my phone buzzed with a message from the advocacy group I led: a video of a local business refusing service to a marginalized family had gone viral, and protesters were gathering, demanding my voice and presence to call out the injustice. I could almost hear their chants, see their expectant faces. My duty as an officer was clear—respond to the robbery, restore order, prevent harm. Yet, as an advocate, I was expected to stand up, to speak out, to be visible in the fight against discrimination. The weight of both uniforms pressed down on me, each demanding my full attention, each refusing to wait. My hands gripped the steering wheel, heart pounding, torn between two urgent calls, each echoing with the voices of those who needed me most.
